brief.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Create ONE finished Japanese basketball editorial thumbnail, landscape 16:9, 1536x864 pixels or larger, PNG. This is a pregame preview illustration, NOT a recreation of a real match or any documented play.

Art direction: follow the approved black-and-lime sports editorial style viewed in this conversation: near-black #151A18 ground, electric lime #CCF43B diagonal dry-brush marks, warm ivory typography, coarse black ink outlines, hand-drawn pen hatching, expressive brush shadow, limited colors. Clearly an illustration, never photographic, never 3D. Few elements, strong hierarchy, powerful mature editorial drawing.

Two real people ONLY: Yusuke Endo (遠藤祐亮), Utsunomiya, and Koya Kawamata (川真田紘也), Ryukyu. They were randomly chosen from their official current rosters; their names, individual statistics, participation or performance claims must NOT appear anywhere in the image. No invented players.
Use these carefully observed official appearance details for likeness:
- Endo, official profile https://www.utsunomiyabrex.com/player_lp/yusuke_endo/ : Japanese adult male, compact strong athletic frame; very short textured spiky hair with bleached light blond tips and dark roots, tightly faded sides, slightly oval squared jaw, defined cheekbones, dark brows, almond eyes, defined straight nose, full lips, neat black moustache connected to a short close-cropped jaw-and-chin beard, small soul patch. Draw his actual recognizable facial structure, not a generic manga face. Plain dark navy sleeveless basketball kit with thin warm yellow edging; NO lettering, NO logos, NO sponsor marks, NO jersey numerals.
- Kawamata, official profile https://goldenkings.jp/team/players/detail/id=25882?PlayerID=5100000015 : Japanese adult male, visibly taller and broader than Endo, sturdy powerful center build; thick medium-short wavy blond hair swept across the top with dark roots and shaved short dark sides; strong broad neck, long oval/squared face, straight thick brows, narrow dark eyes, straight nose, small neat moustache with light beard stubble and defined broad chin. Plain ivory basketball kit with dark navy collar and edging, NO lettering, NO logos, NO sponsor marks, NO jersey numerals.
These profiles and their photos are appearance references only. Do not paste, trace, collage, or reproduce official photos or their backgrounds.

Composition: text fills the left approximately 46%; energetic two-player basketball matchup fills the right approximately 54%. Draw Endo in the right foreground driving diagonally toward the viewer and the left, holding/protecting one orange basketball low beside his hip, knees bent and torso leaning. Draw taller Kawamata opposite and just behind him on the far right, in a credible low defensive stance, one open hand raised and the other arm out, eyes on the ball. Both faces clearly visible in three-quarter view with their distinct hairstyles and facial hair, separated silhouettes, plausible limb joints and five-finger hands. Ball fully inside frame. Frame players from head to upper thighs, deliberately cropping below the thighs if needed, never cutting their faces or hands. No crowd, no additional people, no realistic arena, no scoreboard, no hoop necessary. Keep all elements calm and sparse outside the action. One sweeping lime brush stroke behind the pair creates motion without obscuring faces.

Text, verbatim Japanese and numerals ONLY:
Small upper-left kicker: "試合前展望 / 独自分析"
Huge left headline line 1: "宇都宮"
Huge left headline line 2: "× 琉球"
Below headline, clear bold lime/ivory time: "11/7 16:00"
Bottom left, legible footer: "イラスト（AI生成）"
Next to footer with spacing: "イメージ"
Use thick highly legible Japanese gothic lettering; huge headline with subtle ink texture. No other text at all. Do not carry over Culver, Faison, scores, dates, names, team marks, or typography content from any style reference.
Safe margins at least 5% on every edge; generous clear space behind all text, readable at thumbnail size; footer must remain visible and unobstructed. Text and numbers are supported ONLY by the provided fixed article saying Utsunomiya vs Ryukyu on November 7 at 16:00, pregame preview and independent analysis. Do not add results, points, victory claims, participation predictions, or historical championships.
